title: World Youth Championships day five: three boys' seeds fall as Syndrela Das knocks out Sally Moyland
seo_title: World Youth Championships day 5: three boys' seeds out
description: World Youth Championships day five: Chulong Nie and Aditya Sareen came from behind, Kenan Kahraman beat a seed and Syndrela Das beat Sally Moyland in Istanbul.
standfirst: Australia's Chulong Nie and Aditya Sareen came from behind to beat the third and seventh seeds, and Wen Ruibo and Jiang Yiyi started their singles with wins.
body: Three of the top seven seeds in the boys' singles went out on the first day of the under-19 singles at the World Youth Championships in Istanbul on Wednesday, and India's Syndrela Das beat the girls' seventh seed, Sally Moyland of the United States, in the only match between two players in the world top 100.

The top seeds had a quieter day. China's Wen Ruibo dropped 18 points in a 23-minute win over Italy's Danilo Faso, and Jiang Yiyi lost the first game to Lilian Ma of the United States before winning the next four. All four Chinese players, still chasing four titles each, are in Thursday's last 16, as are the second seeds, Colombia's Emanuel Otalvaro and Japan's Mao Takamori.
## Nie and Sareen come back
The third seed, Kazakhstan's Alan Kurmangaliyev, the world No 131, led Australia's Chulong Nie 3-2 and was beaten 11-3, 11-3 in the last two games. Nie, 19, is ranked 394th.

An hour and a half later his teammate Aditya Sareen, ranked 112th, came from 3-1 down against Taiwan's seventh seed, Lin Chin-Ting. Lin led 3-1 after taking the fourth game 11-7, but Sareen won the last three, 11-7, 11-5 and 11-8. Sareen plays Poland's Samuel Michna next, and Nie plays Tunisia's Wassim Essid, who beat the 14th seed, Ivan Kahn of the Netherlands, 11-7 in the seventh game after 63 minutes, the longest match of the day.
## A home win for Kahraman

The fifth seed, Iran's Benyamin Faraji, lost in straight games to Turkey's Kenan Kahraman, 16, who is ranked 423rd. Three of the four games were close, 13-11, 11-9 and 12-10, before Kahraman took the fourth 11-5. He plays Taiwan's Hung Che-Yen, who beat Li Hechen in Monday's team final, in the last 16.

Kurmangaliyev and Faraji are out of the singles a day before they play together in the boys' doubles semi-finals, against South Korea's Kim Daehwan and Lee Hyeonho. Kim lost his singles 4-0 to Japan's Shunto Iwaida and Lee lost to Michna in five games.
## Das beats Moyland

Das, 17 and ranked 95th, lost the first game to Moyland, the world No 77, and then won four in a row, taking the fifth 11-9. She is one of four Indians in the last 16, with Divyanshi Bhowmick, the eighth seed, who beat Russia's Zlata Terekhova 11-8, 11-8, 11-8, 11-2, Abhinandh Pradhivadhi, the boys' eighth seed, and Priyanuj Bhattacharyya, who now plays Otalvaro. Das meets Taiwan's Wu Jia-En next.

Two other girls' seeds went out. Japan's Aoba Takahashi, the 10th seed, trailed South Korea's Heo Yerim 3-1 and levelled at 3-3, taking the fifth game 11-2 and the sixth 11-7, but Heo, who turned 16 this month, won the seventh 11-6. Heo now plays Egypt's Hana Goda, the world No 21, who beat Hong Kong's Mak Ming Shum 4-0. Germany's Koharu Itagaki, the 14th seed, won the first two games against Poland's Natalia Bogdanowicz, the second 17-15, and lost the next four.

Russia's Eseniia Shirokova beat South Korea's 11th seed, Jeong Yein, 11-9 in the seventh game and plays China's Yao Ruixuan, who beat Austria's Nina Skerbinz 4-0. Takamori dropped 17 points against Poland's Karolina Holda, and Taiwan's Wu Ying Syuan needed 19 minutes to beat New Zealand's Tracey Hsia, the shortest match of the day.

## Thursday: last 16, doubles semi-finals and the mixed doubles final

The singles last 16 starts at about 9.30am UK time. Wen plays Puerto Rico's Steven Moreno, who beat Ramon Vila 11-1 in the seventh game after Vila had come back from 3-1 down, and Jiang plays France's Alexia Nodin. Li Hechen plays Italy's Francesco Trevisan and Yao plays Shirokova, and Takamori meets Australia's Constantina Psihogios, the world No 67.

The boys' and girls' doubles semi-finals follow at about 2.30pm UK time, with Wen and Li against France's Nathan Pilard and Antoine Noirault and Jiang and Yao against Takamori and Takahashi. The under-19 mixed doubles final, between the Chinese pairs Wen and Jiang and Li and Yao, is at about 5pm. Times are approximate. Eleven's [event page](/events/world-youth-championships-2026.html#matches) has live scores and the draws, and the [day five preview](/news/world-youth-championships-2026-day-five-preview-order-of-play.html) has more on the players.
